newsitem.title: USA: Clinton tours flooded area along Potomac.
newsitem.headline: Clinton tours flooded area along Potomac.

text.p: President Clinton Monday got a bird's-eye look at parts of the Potomac River flooded by Hurricane Fran and vowed "quick action" to help people displaced by the disaster.

As Washington itself reeled from Potomac flooding, Clinton flew a helicopter over areas of Virginia and Maryland near the capital and marvelled afterward at "the power, the sheer energy" of the hurricane that hit the North Carolina coast last week and then headed north dumping rain along the way.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with the people who have suffered losses along our Eastern states because of the effects of Hurricane Fran," Clinton told reporters after his tour with Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt and James Lee Witt, director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.

Clinton announced that five additional Virginia counties had been made eligible for federal disaster relief assistance to provide for temporary housing and low-interest loans. They were Mecklenburg, Page, Shenandoah, Rappahanock and Warren.

On his 27-minute tour, Clinton flew over the swollen river at Great Falls, Md., where the Potomac spilled over its banks and wreaked havoc on the C&O Canal tow path, a popular hiking and biking trail just rebuilt after flooding triggered by severe snowstorms early this year. Clinton and Vice President Al Gore had helped clean up debris from the path last spring.
"Much of that work will now have to be done again because it's been undone by the flooding," he said.

Clinton also saw areas of Old Town Alexandria, Va., hit by flooding of the Potomac and Hains Point in the capital where he often jogs. As for another hurricane brewing in the Caribbean, Hortense, Clinton said "we'll just watch it" and be prepared with federal aid if necessary.

"We'll have to afford as many as we have to sustain," he added. He said he doubted Republicans would quibble with the disaster aid budget, saying, "I think Americans without regard to party believe in aggressive disaster relief."
Clinton said people who may qualify for federal disaster aid should call 1-800-462-9029. Those wanting to make donations to help people recover should call 1-800-747-8920.
